correctness.rationale: Every hypothesis and quantifier is explicit: a finite or countable squared-norm-summable Kraus family, any complex Hilbert space, every integer word length m>=1, and Banach ideals B(H), K(H), S_p for 1<=p<infinity. An orthonormal weak-null sequence gives a necessary compactness test and finite-rank approximations give sufficiency on every ideal. Powers have word Kraus families with convergent square-norm sums. The same finite-dimensional compression gives finite-rank approximants to both powers on all ideals. Hilbert-Schmidt adjointness plus antilinear *-symmetry gives identical nonzero characteristic roots, with Riesz spectral-projection stability preserving algebraic multiplicity in the compact limits. Complete positivity and Gelfand give row and column radii from Kraus map spectral radii. Both explicit boundary examples are checked algebraically. The packaged script passed 622 supplemental tests; these are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary source proves equal row/column radii for finite matrix tuples and gives unrestricted infinite-dimensional counterexamples. Its Kraus-map argument does not cover the precise power-compact recovery class. The later 2026 source reinforces the finite/infinite distinction but has a different operator-space classification aim. The 1979 compact elementary-operator theorem was inspected and is credited; compactness of elementary operators is not presented as independently new. The distinct candidate result is the simultaneous fixed-word compactness criterion, full B(H)/K(H)/S_p nonzero Riesz-multiset transfer for compact powers, and row-column recovery on noncompact generating families. No source inspected states or logically subsumes that combined assertion. Some standard ingredients are classical and possible equivalent older synthesis remains a risk. Three closely related published mathematical claims were also read in full, including the strongest elementary-operator compactness result and the two operator-space radius distortion theorems. Their hypotheses/conclusions differ and none implies the new compact-word spectral transfer.

value.rationale: Scherer–Shalit–Shamovich give a sharp qualitative finite-versus-unrestricted-infinite dichotomy for the operator-space row and column radii. The finding identifies a natural infinite-dimensional boundary where finite spectral behavior is restored: all sufficiently long words compact, equivalent to both completely positive maps being power compact on every Banach Schatten ideal. This condition strictly exceeds having compact generators; a noncompact noncommuting family with nonzero radius realizes the distinction. Equality of full nonzero Riesz spectra and multiplicities is stronger than radius equality. The Cuntz-isometry example proves that unrestricted tuples cannot be covered. The result is a structural classification and transfer principle, not a numerically small improvement, arbitrary sample, or textbook parameter substitution.
